schema.title: Validate the facts and eligibility, not just the JSON.

aeo.title: Treat readiness as an input and observed answers as a separate test.

content.title: Every brief needs an audience, a commercial job, and a QA owner.

authority.title: Earn evidence that makes the brand easier to trust.

community.title: Useful participation comes before a mention target.
community.description: Listen to the questions, respect each community’s rules, disclose relevant relationships, and contribute where there is real expertise. Measure referrals and mentions without claiming that a post caused AI inclusion.

shopping.title: Fix eligibility and feed truth before testing presentation.
shopping.description: Validate Merchant Center diagnostics, identifiers, price and stock consistency, and free-listing eligibility. Then test product titles or images in a controlled cohort with account data.

cro.title: Use business outcomes to refine the search opportunity.
cro.description: For Shopify clients, connect landing-page cohorts to transactions, net revenue, inventory, and margin. For the SEOasis agency site, track qualified leads and booked calls as a separate funnel.

competitors.title: The differentiator has to survive beyond the headline.
competitors.description: AI/AEO messaging appears across the sampled peer set. Make the fulfillment model tangible through collection briefs, accountable QA, direct communication, and documented quarterly learning.

measurement.title: Report the decision, not just the metric.
measurement.description: Agree on baselines, attribution, and definitions before connecting platforms. Every weekly update and client report should explain what changed, what remains uncertain, and the next action with an owner.

scope.method: Serial curl GET of 20 sitemap-selected pages; raw HTML parsed with Python standard library.
limitations: Purposive sample, not a complete crawl.
Source HTML only; browser rendering not tested.
HTTP 200 and no robots block do not prove Google indexation.
No GSC, GA4, backlink database, rankings, field CWV or revenue data accessed.
Linked targets outside this sample were not status-checked; no site-wide broken-link conclusion.
Image bytes and decoded dimensions not downloaded; HTML response size is not image weight.
JSON parse success is not a Google Rich Results or Schema.org validation result.
scope.coverage: 20 purposively selected HTML pages plus robots.txt and sitemap.xml; not a complete crawl.

findings.evidence: 20/20 sampled pages returned final HTTP 200 and one H1. All 20 source pages include index, follow robots meta. robots.txt allows / and references a 70-URL sitemap. This establishes public accessibility, not Google indexation.
findings.businessImplication: Existing public access gives an operator a useful starting point; search-engine selected canonicals and actual index coverage still need verification.
findings.recommendedAction: Preserve these controls; join sitemap URLs to Search Console Page indexing and URL Inspection samples before claiming indexed coverage.

findings.issue: Case-study canonical consistency is worth validating
findings.evidence: No rel=canonical link appeared in server-delivered HTML on the case-study hub and the three sampled case studies; the remaining 16 sampled pages expose a canonical. Omission alone does not establish duplication or indexation loss.
findings.businessImplication: A consistent preferred-URL signal may help maintain the proof-content library as URL variants grow.
findings.recommendedAction: Check Google-selected canonical and any URL variants; if preferred URLs are confirmed, implement an absolute self-canonical through the shared case-study template and QA it.

findings.issue: Repeated brand suffix in sampled title templates
findings.evidence: 7 of 20 sampled titles end with the exact repeated suffix '| SEOasis | SEOasis'. Example: Shopify SEO Agency Built for AI Search | SEOasis | SEOasis. Natural mentions of SEOasis in a title subject are excluded; this is repeated branding within a title, not duplicate titles across URLs.
findings.businessImplication: Removing redundant branding could improve title clarity; CTR impact remains unmeasured.
findings.recommendedAction: Remove the repeated suffix in the shared title/template source, confirm unique intent-focused titles, then monitor query-adjusted CTR in Search Console.

findings.issue: Homepage commercial discovery paths merit a controlled test
findings.evidence: Homepage source HTML exposes four distinct internal destinations after fragments are removed: /, /case-studies, /privacy-policy and /terms-of-service. The sitemap contains 70 URLs including /shopify-seo-agency, /ecommerce-seo and /blog. This sample does not establish sitewide orphan pages or actual crawl depth.
findings.businessImplication: Relevant service/resource links could help visitors discover the operating model and provide more explicit commercial pathways.
findings.recommendedAction: Validate the complete rendered link graph, then test a restrained service/resource pathway from the homepage or shared navigation; connect relevant case studies contextually.

findings.issue: Structured data is already present across most sampled templates
findings.evidence: 19/20 sampled pages contain parseable JSON-LD. Homepage includes Organization, ProfessionalService, WebSite and additional types; commercial templates include Service/FAQPage; case studies Article; sampled posts BlogPosting/Person. The ChatGPT visibility audit page has no JSON-LD detected. JSON parse success does not validate Google eligibility or claim accuracy.
findings.businessImplication: QA can focus on eligible, accurate markup and visible-content parity instead of assuming schema needs to be introduced from scratch.
findings.recommendedAction: Run representative templates through Schema.org and Rich Results validators; review IDs, factual claims, visible-content parity and Google feature-specific restrictions before changing markup.

findings.issue: Image alt attributes exist throughout the sample
findings.evidence: 75 img elements across 20 sampled HTML pages all include an alt attribute. Presence does not establish useful alternative text; empty alt may be appropriate for decorative images. Image byte weight was not tested.
findings.businessImplication: An accessibility/content review should examine meaning and decorative treatment rather than assigning a blanket missing-alt task.
findings.recommendedAction: Keep the attribute coverage; manually review representative alt text in context and inspect downloaded image dimensions/weight only if performance evidence warrants it.

findings.issue: One sampled description ends mid-phrase in the HTML
findings.evidence: The source meta description ends: tracks real results. Not vanity me. This incomplete ending is in source HTML; it is not an observation of a Google snippet.
findings.businessImplication: A complete, concise description would communicate the article promise more clearly; Google may choose a different snippet.
findings.recommendedAction: Replace the incomplete phrase with a complete intent-matched description and inspect the published source. Measure query-adjusted CTR only after a baseline exists.

findings.issue: Index coverage and performance remain unvalidated
findings.evidence: Requires Internal Access. No Search Console, GA4, Shopify, Merchant Center or private crawler account was accessed. Public field Core Web Vitals and a browser mobile/rendered audit were not collected in this bounded HTTP workstream.
findings.businessImplication: Public HTML cannot establish indexation, organic traffic, conversions, revenue, selected canonicals, real-user performance or priority based on business outcomes.
findings.recommendedAction: Pull Search Console Page indexing, sitemap processing, URL Inspection and query/page performance; GA4 landing-page outcomes; use PageSpeed Insights/CrUX when accessible. Let verified indexation/performance and revenue exposure determine remediation order.
findings.platform: Google Search Console; GA4; public PageSpeed Insights/CrUX for performance
findings.metric: Indexed/canonical status, clicks/impressions/CTR, landing-page conversions, field LCP/INP/CLS
findings.decision: Whether technical remediation or acquisition/conversion work should lead the 90-day plan

limitations: Purposive sample, not a complete crawl.
Source HTML only; browser rendering not tested.
HTTP 200 and no robots block do not prove Google indexation.
No GSC, GA4, backlink database, rankings, field CWV or revenue data accessed.
Linked targets outside this sample were not status-checked; no site-wide broken-link conclusion.

No redirect-variant matrix, mobile interaction, pagination or full external/internal target status sweep was performed.
